'''José-Antonio Campos-Ortega''' (22 August 1940 – 8 May 2004)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Knust |first=Elisabeth |last2=Hertel |first2=Rainer |date=2009 |title=Jose-Antonio Campos-Ortega (1940-2004) and his scientific work - a personal perspective |url=https://ijdb.ehu.eus/article/072480ek |journal=The International Journal of Developmental Biology |language=en |volume=53 |issue=8-9-10 |pages=1193–1203 |doi=10.1387/ijdb.072480ek |issn=0214-6282}}</ref> was a Spanish [[Neurobiology|neurobiologist]] born in [[Valencia|Valencia, Spain]] shortly after the [[Spanish Civil War]].<ref name="Roberto 2006">{{cite journal |last=Marco |first=Roberto |date=Apr 2006 |title=The scientific roots of José A. Campos-Ortega, a German neurobiologist born in Spain |journal=[[Developmental Dynamics|Dev. Dyn.]] |location=United States |volume=235 |issue=4 |pages=855–60 |doi=10.1002/dvdy.20700 |pmid=16496283 |doi-access=free}}<!-- Author knew and worked with Campos-Ortega. --></ref> He was known as a pioneer of developmental-genetic studies of early [[neurogenesis]].

Campos-Ortega attended a [[Dominican Order|Dominican]] [[religious school]] for his [[Education in Spain|secondary education]] (roughly ages 12 to 16).<ref name="Roberto 2006" />  In 1958 (at 18) he started studying medicine, which had been a tradition in his family and a financial necessity in Spain of the period; this pursuit was at the cost of setting aside his burgeoning interest in histology and research.<ref name="Roberto 2006" />
